sections.overview: Hartweg’s Sphinx is a Sphingidae moth of the south-western United States, Mexico and Guatemala; the related-family entry Dolba hyloeus is profiled separately.
sections.identification: Its forewings are brown with dark and white markings and a pale round spot; the wingspan is about 54–61 mm.
sections.habitat: Records place it in the south-western United States and Mexico, with additional records in Guatemala.
sections.diet: A rearing study identified Tecoma stans as a larval host plant in Arizona and Mexico.
sections.behavior: Adults have been recorded in July and August, though the observed flight period may extend beyond those months.
sections.reproduction: The caterpillar and its host plant were documented in a published rearing and field observation; broader reproductive details remain sparse.
sections.ecology: The confirmed Tecoma association is the clearest published host relationship found in the sources consulted.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted do not provide a species-specific conservation assessment, and note that relatively few specimens have been reported.
